title: Filed Short-Rate Table: Percentage Retained When the Named Insured Cancels an Owner Auto Policy
content:
**Table.** When an Owner Auto Policy term is cancelled at the named insured's request, the company's filed short-rate table sets the percentage retained from the unearned premium. It reads two things:
- the request reason on the request handled;
- the days from the term effective date to the cancellation effective date, with the term effective date counted and the cancellation effective date not counted.

| Request reason | Days into the term at cancellation | Percentage retained |
|---|---|---|
| Moved out of state, vehicle sold or totaled, or no longer driving | any | nothing (the risk has ended; returned pro rata) |
| Any other reason | fewer than 60 | the package's short-rate retention percentage |
| Any other reason | 60 or more | half the package's short-rate retention percentage |

The percentage acts once on the unearned premium.

**The package's short-rate retention percentage.** This is set in the return premium methods table:

| Package | Package percentage | Half of it |
|---|---|---|
| Cardinal Point Minimum Limits Liability, 50/100/50, 100/200/50 and 100/300/50 Liability | 10 | 5 |
| Cardinal Point 100/300/100 and 250/500/100 Liability | 0 | 0 |

**Both sides of the day threshold (hypothetical: a package with a 10 percent retention, and a reason other than the three listed).**
- Taking effect on day 59: 10 percent is retained.
- Taking effect on day 60: 5 percent is retained.

**Points of judgement.**
- A request recording the reason "vehicle sold or totaled" retains nothing, whatever the day count.
- A request with no recorded reason falls under "any other reason".
